expectations.text: States the scheme basics correctly: NCSC-owned, delivered through IASME and licensed certification bodies; verified self-assessment signed off by a board member and marked by an assessor; certificates valid 12 months with annual renewal
expectations.evidence: No NCSC ownership mentioned; has 'Purchase the assessment through IASME or a licensed Certification Body', 'A board member... signs a declaration', 'valid for 12 months' but omits NCSC-owned element

expectations.text: Uses the CURRENT question set: assessment accounts created from April 27, 2026 use the Danzell question set / Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3 (not Willow, which only applies to earlier accounts in a closing transition window)
expectations.evidence: 'from 27 April 2026 onward, you'll be assessed against the current "Danzell" question set (Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3)'; Willow only 'If your account predates that date'

expectations.text: Prices it correctly for a 40-person company: £440 + VAT (small, 10-49 employees) for basic CE, with CE Plus separately quoted
expectations.evidence: 'Pricing for your size band (10-49 staff, "small"): £440 + VAT'; CE Plus 'is quoted separately'

expectations.text: Covers the five control themes by name: firewalls, secure configuration, security update management, user access control, malware protection
expectations.evidence: 'firewalls..., secure configuration..., security update management..., user access control..., and malware protection'

expectations.text: Flags the automatic-fail conditions under Danzell: MFA missing on cloud services where available, and the 14-day high/critical update questions — plus mentions the government-contract context (PPN 014 requires CE or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: 'two automatic-fail conditions... (1) missing MFA on any cloud service... (2)... 14-day critical-update rule... (A6.4)... (A6.5)'; 'under PPN 014'
